newsitem.title: USA: Maine Yankee power plant might restart in Aug - NRC.
newsitem.headline: Maine Yankee power plant might restart in Aug - NRC.

text.p: The Maine Yankee nuclear plant may restart this August, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Thursday in its plant status report.
Operators at the 910 megawatt plant are expected to replace 92 fuel bundles, which will be received in July, the NRC report stated.
The plant, in Wiscasset, Maine, was shut in December to correct electrical cable problems affecting back-up systems.
In late January, it was placed on the NRC's watchlist following a series of unplanned outages over the past two years.
A plant spokesman was not immediately available to confirm the August restart.
Earlier this month a Maine Yankee official declined to speculate on when the plant likely would resume operation.
Maine Yankee is responsible for supplying about a quarter of the state's electricity.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co, and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
